**The Cato Corporation - Fourth Amendment to Credit Agreement**

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** April 25, 2024

**Borrower / Company Overview:** The Cato Corporation, a Delaware corporation

**Transaction Description:** Fourth Amendment to Credit Agreement originally dated May 19, 2022, among The Cato Corporation, certain domestic subsidiaries, various banks and financial institutions, with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association serving as Agent, Issuing Bank and as a Bank.

**Purpose of Financing:** Amendment to modify the definition of Minimum EBITDAR Coverage Ratio covenant to provide more favorable covenant calculation for the borrower, specifically allowing for income tax receivable addbacks of up to $5.325 million related to 2021 fiscal year tax refunds.

**Company Background and Context:** Based on the amendment history (First Amendment June 6, 2022; Second Amendment August 9, 2023; Third Amendment October 24, 2023; Fourth Amendment April 25, 2024), The Cato Corporation appears to be actively managing its credit facility terms, suggesting potential financial covenant management needs.

---

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
• **Established Banking Relationship:** Borrower maintains ongoing relationship with Wells Fargo as administrative agent and participant bank
• **Covenant Flexibility:** Lenders willing to provide covenant relief, indicating potential for continued partnership
• **Clean Legal Standing:** Borrower confirms no knowledge of claims or litigation against lenders as of amendment date
• **Structured Amendment Process:** Formal amendment process demonstrates adherence to credit agreement procedures

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• **Covenant Pressure:** Fourth amendment in less than two years suggests ongoing financial covenant challenges
• **Income Tax Dependency:** Amendment relies on anticipated tax receivables ($5.325 million maximum) for covenant relief, introducing execution risk
• **Temporary Relief:** Tax receivable addback expires after Q2 2024 or upon receipt of refunds, providing only short-term covenant relief
• **Limited Visibility:** Amendment document provides minimal insight into underlying business performance or financial condition
